html:
In 1997 Kazakhstan moved its capital from Almaty in the far southeast to the small northern city of Aqmola, renamed Astana, "capital", the next year.

The town began in 1830 as a Russian fort, Akmolinsk. It became the centre of the Virgin Lands campaign of the 1950s to plough the steppe, and was renamed Tselinograd in 1961. President Nursultan Nazarbayev gave reasons for the move: Almaty sits in an earthquake zone, near the borders, with little room to grow. Many also saw a wish to anchor the north, where most people were ethnic Russians.

Oil money built a new city on the windy steppe. The Japanese architect Kisho Kurokawa drew the master plan, and Norman Foster designed a glass pyramid and a giant tent shaped shopping centre. The Bayterek tower became the city's symbol. From 2019 to 2022 the city was called Nur-Sultan after Nazarbayev, before taking back the name Astana.
sum: In 1997 Kazakhstan moved its capital from Almaty in the far southeast to the small northern city of Aqmola, renamed Astana, "capital", the next year.
